purpose: Levofloxacin is an antibiotic used to treat bacterial infections such as pneumonia, sinus infections, urinary tract infections, and skin infections. It is also sometimes used to treat or prevent anthrax exposure. It only works against bacterial infections and will not help with viral illnesses like the common cold or flu.
how_it_works: Levofloxacin works by blocking special enzymes that bacteria need to copy and repair their DNA. Without these enzymes, the bacteria cannot reproduce or survive and they eventually die off. Think of it like cutting off a key tool the bacteria need to keep going.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, diarrhea, headache, dizziness, and trouble sleeping. Some people may notice constipation or stomach upset. These side effects are usually mild and often go away as your body adjusts to the medication.
warnings: This medication carries an important warning about a rare but serious risk of tendon damage, especially in the Achilles tendon at the back of your heel — stop taking it and call your doctor right away if you feel sudden pain or swelling in a tendon. It can also cause nerve damage, mood changes, or irregular heart rhythms in some people. Avoid taking it with antacids, dairy products, or calcium-fortified drinks within 2 hours of your dose. People over 60, those on steroids, or those with kidney problems are at higher risk for tendon problems. Always let your doctor know all the medications you take.
typical_dosing: The typical adult dose is 250 mg to 750 mg taken once daily by mouth, depending on the type and severity of your infection. It is best taken at the same time each day, with or without food, and with a full glass of water. Drink plenty of fluids throughout the day. Always finish the full course of antibiotics even if you start feeling better.
